messages.subject: [rJava] [SOLVED] overload decimal separator
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

here is a digest of my discussion with Simon concerning the following bug :

I was using a french locale for my Java installation, so when loading 
rJava, the LC_NUMERIC field (you can see in Sys.getLocale()) was reset 
to fr_FR.UTF-8.
Then, when typing "1.1" in the command line, it was returning me "1,1" 
(with a comma, which is the french decimal separator).

The diagnosis suggested by Simon (despite my unprecise question :) was 
that the LC_NUMERIC field was changed by the loading of Java.
He was right, so the turn-around is the following  : after having loaded 
rJava and called .jinit(), do not forget to set back your LC_NUMERIC 
field to the decimal separator you wish (usually "C", by default for R):

 > Sys.setlocale(category="LC_NUMERIC",locale="C")

Thank you Simon !

Yann

-- 
Dr. Yann Richet
Scientific Advisor - Applied Mathematics,
Neutronics and Criticality Safety Assessment Department,
Institute for Radiological Protection and Nuclear Safety,
office: +33 1 58 35 88 84

messages.subject: iPlots Java source code licence
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
in a Java SWT application, we need to add semantic data to some plots 
generated by R. At the moment, we're looking at the iPlots package and 
at the possiblity to embed it in the application.

The toolkit doesn't seem to offer all the functions for our needs. We 
need to, for example, create new graph types, add custom Java GUI 
components (as menus, tooltips, translate the entries if we keep some of 
existent ones, etc.) and to capture/add custom Java events from the 
iPlots Window/Canvas components (eg. bars, points of scatters, etc.).
After some research, it appears the better way could be to modify the 
Java source code of the iplots.jar package if we want to do this (I 
think extend it may not be enough for our needs).

Could you tell us if the Java source code is distributed and if so, 
under which license ? (the Java source code is not on Cran)

If the licence is compatible, do you think is it possible to embed 
iPlots in an other Java application in easy way ? iPlot seems to run his 
own JVM inside R process and I guess it'll may be difficult to embed the 
iPlots canvas in existent Java GUI components in already run Java 
application.

Thanks in advance for these precisions.

Cheers,
Sebastian

--

messages.body_plain:
Sebastian,

On Sep 12, 2013, at 3:28 AM, Centre Jacques-Petit wrote:

> Hello,
> in a Java SWT application, we need to add semantic data to some plots generated by R. At the moment, we're looking at the iPlots package and at the possiblity to embed it in the application.
> 
> The toolkit doesn't seem to offer all the functions for our needs. We need to, for example, create new graph types, add custom Java GUI components (as menus, tooltips, translate the entries if we keep some of existent ones, etc.) and to capture/add custom Java events from the iPlots Window/Canvas components (eg. bars, points of scatters, etc.).
> After some research, it appears the better way could be to modify the Java source code of the iplots.jar package if we want to do this (I think extend it may not be enough for our needs).
> 

Your statements are somewhat surprising. iPlots have been designed specifically to allow very easy ways to extend it and create new plot types. The framework is highly modular, new plot types are easy to create (have a look at the icp package that even allows you to do that direct from R without any Java code) and new primitives can be added by simple subclassing. I would recommend familiarizing yourself with the design of the framework if possible (probably the most extensive description is in Chapter 4 of "Exploratory Model Analysis: An Interactive Graphical Framework for Model Comparison and Selection", more recent overview if iPlots eXtreme which holds true for the most part for the older iPlots as well is in the iPlots eXtreme DSC paper http://urbanek.info/pub/dsc09.pdf ). Let me know if you have any questions, I'd be happy to help.


> Could you tell us if the Java source code is distributed and if so, under which license ? (the Java source code is not on Cran)
> 

The sources are available under GPLv2 (see the package).
http://www.rforge.net/iplots/svn.html


> If the licence is compatible, do you think is it possible to embed iPlots in an other Java application in easy way ? iPlot seems to run his own JVM inside R process and I guess it'll may be difficult to embed the iPlots canvas in existent Java GUI components in already run Java application.
> 

Not at all - see JGR - it embeds both R and iPlots into a Java application. If you wanted, you could do even without the R process since iPlots use it only for R-side extensibility.

Cheers,
Simon


> Thanks in advance for these precisions.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've developed an R script and want to call it from a java app using the 
Rserve. the script works and takes for a single input file around 20 
mins. More input files require more times but linear.

It works perfectly if i use a single file. The problem is in case of 
multiple input files, where more time required.  The parseAndEval method 
of the RConnection starts the execution of the R script and then waits 
for the execution finishing. Even though the script run successfully and 
finish, the parseAndEval method never returns, just waits forever.

I've tried the the keep.alive option (added to the Rserv.conf as 
'keep.alive enable'), did not help. Same problem with the previous and 
the newest versions.

Has anyone experiencied such a similar problem? How to solve this? How 
can i debug this problem?

Ubuntu 12.04.3 64bit, R 3.0.1
Thanks a lot,
ilhami

messages.subject_clean: REngine Dual instance ends up killing both of them
messages.body_plain:
Manish,

I guess you're talking about JRI and not REngine. R is single-threaded, so you can only run one JRIEngine instance in one JVM (and you can only initialize it once). If you want parallel connections, consider using Rserve (REngine supports both JRI and Rserve). For R-based web-services, have a look at FastRWeb (which uses Rserve).

Cheers,
Simon
